name: Chicken Cacciatore (Italian Chicken Stew)
method: braise (stovetop, browned then simmered in red-wine tomato sauce)
ingredients_verbatim: 4 bone in chicken thighs (large, 1 kg / 2 lb)
2 rosemary sprigs (about 15 cm/6 inch long), or 1 tsp dried rosemary
2 bay leaves, preferably fresh else dried
3 anchovy fillets (or 1 tsp anchovy paste), optional
2 red capsicum (red bell pepper), sliced 8 mm thick (medium, not giant)
3/4 cup pinot noir or other dry red wine
Mashed potato or polenta (serving, side only)
main_ingredients: chicken thighs (bone-in in source; rebuild on boneless-skinless-chicken-thigh)
why: Genuine low-carb chicken braise (RTE labels method 'Braising'): browned chicken simmered in red-wine tomato-mushroom-pepper sauce, no pasta/rice/potato in the dish itself. Published 495 cal / 37g protein / 15g carbs per serving sits in the middle of the band with margin under both the 650-cal and 35g-carb ceilings. Distinct from the catalog's slow-cooker-chicken-cacciatore-PASTA (that one is starch-heavy, oven/slow method); this is the classic stovetop stew. Cacciatore-style is explicitly named in-lane. Every signature ingredient (red-wine, kalamata-olives, anchovies) maps to the Omaha board, so it prices cleanly at 14 servings. High confidence: nutrition read directly from source page.
